newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil prices end with steep gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil prices end with steep gains.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil prices ended Friday with steep gains stoked by supply concerns in the United States and Europe, while October crude oil set a closing high partly on short covering, traders said.
"The reason heating oil outperformed was on the legitimate concern that supplies are tight here and in Europe," said Tom Bentz, a trader with ING Derivatives.
October heat closed up 1.37 cents to 66.40 cents a gallon.
American Petroleum Institute's latest weekly data showed distillate stocks 14 percent below year ago, and traders expect upcoming diesel exports to further tighten supply.
September gas oil settled $7 higher at $219.75 cents a tonne on London's IPE Friday, 75 cents off the day's high.
October heating oil is poised to test resistance pegged at 67.00 cents, and 67.50 after that, traders said.
October crude oil settled 41 cents higher, marking a closing high of $23.85 a barrel. The contract high is $24.25 set Tuesday on the Iraqi conflict.
"There was late stage short covering after crude went weaker but then wouldn't breakdown," said ING's Bentz.
October gasoline settled up 0.86 cent to 65.27 cents a gallon.
Gasoline is considered the least compelling leg of the oil complex, traders said, and they expect its price to take direction from crude and heating oil.
The October gasoline-to-crude crack spread narrowed slightly compared with Thursday as traders said longs favored crude's prospects over gasoline's.
"All the indicators are finding a comfort zone above $23.00," said a trader of crude's price.
With heating oil's rise igniting crude's rise today, traders said crude's uptrend will be pinned partly to continued supply tighteness in heating oil as well as developments in Iraq.
Dealers pegged resistance for October crude at around $23.95 a barrel, the contract's intraday high set Tuesday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
